title: Power of the Master Mind: The Driving Force
coreMove: Build power by organizing knowledge through a small, reciprocal alliance that shares a definite purpose and protects harmony while work moves.

exampleSpecs.audience: operators who confuse personal expertise with organized power
exampleSpecs.stakes: a steel supplier can win the bid only if separate specialties become one offer
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show Andrew Carnegie's steel alliance as organized specialized minds, not one person's private genius

exampleSpecs.audience: founders building peer circles for stimulation rather than status
exampleSpecs.stakes: choose advisers who change the quality of thought before a retreat calendar closes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Ford's association with Edison, Firestone, and Burroughs to show chosen mental company

exampleSpecs.audience: small teams whose alliance looks strong on paper but brittle in practice
exampleSpecs.stakes: the agreement gets signed only if the relational condition is repaired
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show that two or more people need harmony, definite purpose, and cooperation

exampleSpecs.audience: builders who have facts but no organized means
exampleSpecs.stakes: a second investor meeting needs directed knowledge instead of better wishes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show power as organized and intelligently directed knowledge

exampleSpecs.audience: networkers who mistake friendly access for alliance power
exampleSpecs.stakes: a pleasant group either names a shared aim or remains scattered advice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show that an alliance must be tied to a definite purpose

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders pruning a large contact list into a serious thinking circle
exampleSpecs.stakes: the final invitation list has to create stimulation, not just attendance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show Ford's association with Edison, Firestone, and Burroughs as chosen mental company
